title: BroadcastSession
description: One broadcast: a call or a recording made watchable from outside the room it happens in, planned in advance or started on the spot. It is a separate record from CallSession because a broadcast has a different audience (the people watching, not the people in the call), can be paused while the call goes on, can exist before any call does, and can have a one-person recording as its source, with no call at all. STATE IS READ FROM FACTS; there is no status field. The broadcast HAPPENED if and only if `startedAt` is present. It is OVER when `endedAt` is present; a reader that cannot ask the broadcasting platform also treats it as over once `until` has passed, and writes nothing. `endedAt` without `startedAt` means nothing. A broadcast planned in its own record and called off carries `cancelledAt`; one planned as part of an Event is called off by cancelling that Event. A past `startsAt` with no `startedAt` and no cancellation means it should have started and did not — a reader must not infer cancellation from the clock. THE PLAN LIVES IN ONE PLACE. When the broadcast belongs to an Event (`eventId` + `eventOwnerEName`), its title and times are the Event's, and this record carries no `title`, `startsAt` or `endsAt` of its own. Without an Event, those fields here are the plan. The Event's ACL is independent of this record's: a broadcast with `eventId` requires that Event to be readable by this record's audience; when the organiser cannot ensure that, the broadcast carries its own `title` as well, so its audience is never shown a broadcast without a name. WHO WRITES WHAT, in two disjoint groups: the plan (`title`, `eventId`, `eventOwnerEName`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`, `cancelledAt`, `cancellationReason`) is written by whoever created the record; the live fields (`startedAt`, `endedAt`, `until`, `watchUrl`, `source`, `intervals`) only by the platform that runs the broadcast, and every other application reads them. An update replaces the top-level keys it sends and keeps the rest, so the two groups cannot overwrite each other. This is a contract between writers, not something the vault enforces. The transcript and summary of what was ON AIR — only the stretches in `intervals`, never the talk before, after or between them — are a Summary whose `subject.ref` is this record. Such a Summary is derived only from what the broadcast's audience already saw, so it is no more public than its source; it carries no action items. This record's ACL is the broadcast's audience. Putting a group's call on air widens its audience beyond the group, which is publishing rather than running the group; that is why this type sits in the `media` domain, so that permission to broadcast is granted visibly and separately. It is stored on the vault that holds the Chat named in `chat`: the chat of the call, or for a recording the chat the recording is posted in — there is always one.

id.description: Stable id of the broadcast (UUIDv4). Unchanged for the life of the record.

chat.description: Envelope URI (vault and envelope id, not the body id) of the Chat whose call is broadcast, or in which the broadcast recording is posted — the chat of the people on air, not any chat the broadcast is shared into.

title.description: What is being broadcast, as the audience should see it. Absent when `eventId` is set and that Event is readable by this record's audience; present otherwise.

eventId.description: The stable `eventId` from the body of the Event (a programme item) this broadcast belongs to — not its envelope id, which changes with every edit of the Event. Set together with `eventOwnerEName`; the reader finds the CURRENT version of the Event by this id on that vault: among the records carrying this `eventId`, the one that no other record names in its `supersedes`. Taking the first match instead would show an old time. Deliberately not pinned to one envelope: a programme item that moves must move its broadcast with it. When set, the Event is the plan: its title, times and cancellation.

eventOwnerEName.description: eName of the vault holding that Event, so the reader can find it by `eventId`.

startsAt.description: When the broadcast is planned to begin. Absent for a broadcast started on the spot, and when `eventId` is set.

endsAt.description: When it is planned to end. Absent when `eventId` is set.

cancelledAt.description: When a broadcast planned in this record was called off. Not used when `eventId` is set: the Event's own cancellation is the fact.

cancellationReason.description: Why it was called off, for the audience. Present only with `cancelledAt`.

startedAt.description: When it first went on air. Its presence, and nothing else, means the broadcast happened.

endedAt.description: When it was taken off air for good. Absent while it may still continue.

until.description: A lease for readers that cannot ask the broadcasting platform: past this instant the broadcast is over even if `endedAt` never arrived. The broadcasting platform extends it while on air.

watchUrl.description: Where to watch: a page of the broadcasting platform that admits viewers against this record's audience. After the broadcast it says that it has ended.

source.description: What is broadcast: a call, or one person's recording.

intervals.description: The stretches that were actually on air, oldest first. A pause ends one; a resume starts the next. The list is replaced whole on every update: a writer adding a stretch reads the record first and writes the full list back.

id.description: Stable id of this stretch, so it can be referred to without its position in the list.

startedAt.description: When this stretch went on air.

endedAt.description: When it stopped, by a pause or the end. Absent while on air.

call.description: Envelope URI of the CallSession on air during this stretch, when `source` is call. A call that dropped and was started again continues the same broadcast in a new stretch with a new CallSession.

recording.description: Envelope URI of the record holding the recording on air during this stretch, when `source` is recording.

createdByEName.description: eName of the person who created the broadcast (pressed the button or planned it).
